author: K. J. Gordon
title: MLB Pipeline highlights top catching prospects ahead of release of Top 100 list
text:
Busch Stadium | St. Louis Cardinals
Busch Stadium | St. Louis Cardinals
MLB Pipeline has announced that its 2026 Top 100 Prospects list will be revealed on January 23 at 8 p.m. ET, with coverage available on MLB Network and MLB.com. In the days leading up to the full list, the organization is highlighting the top 10 prospects at each position.
Despite several notable catchers, including Drake Baldwin, Edgar Quero, Dalton Rushing, and Kyle Teel, moving up to Major League Baseball in 2025, catching prospects continue to show depth across the league. The upcoming Top 100 Prospects list will feature 12 catchers, just one fewer than last year’s record.
Four of these catchers are considered strong candidates for Rookie of the Year in 2026: Samuel Basallo (Orioles) and Carter Jensen (Royals) in the American League; Moisés Ballesteros (Cubs) and Joe Mack (Marlins) in the National League.
No catcher selected in the previous two drafts made it into this year’s Top 100. However, Rainiel Rodriguez of the Cardinals signed during the international signing period in 2024. Of the top ten catching prospects, six entered professional baseball through international signings while four were selected within the first three rounds of their respective drafts.
The analysis highlights several skills among these prospects:
- Moisés Ballesteros and Carter Jensen are recognized for their hitting abilities.
- Samuel Basallo and Rainiel Rodriguez stand out for their power at bat.
- Harry Ford is noted for his speed compared to other catchers.
- Basallo also possesses a strong throwing arm.
- Joe Mack and Mitchell are highlighted for their defensive skills.
Basallo is seen as having the highest potential ceiling among catchers due to his combination of offensive power and a strong arm. "Basallo could be a .275 hitter with 35 or more homers per year, which would make him an All-Star even if he doesn't stay behind the plate. It will be interesting to see if he can gain enough defensive polish to stick at catcher and whether the Orioles may want to maximize his offensive production by moving him elsewhere."
Joe Mack is described as having a high floor because of his defense: "At worst, Mack's defensive prowess alone should translate into a long career as a backup. And while he's a true power-over-hit guy, adjustments at the plate have enabled him to total 45 homers in the last two seasons."
Regarding rookie honors next season, Basallo leads projections but Ballesteros and Jensen are also mentioned as players likely to get significant playing time: "Basallo is the most obvious choice here, but Ballesteros and Jensen are two more gifted hitters with nothing left to prove in the Minors. All three should get regular big league at-bats in 2026, though a lot of them may come at DH. Mack is a far better defender than Marlins incumbent Agustín Ramírez and ready for his chance to start in the Majors."
Rodriguez is identified as making significant progress over recent seasons after signing with St. Louis during an international period: "Rodriguez had the lowest profile a year ago because he had yet to advance past the Dominican Summer League, though he did rank second in the Rookie circuit in slugging (.683) and OPS (1.145) in his debut."
Tait stands out for coming from modest beginnings before being traded from Philadelphia to Minnesota: "Tait originally signed with the Phillies for a modest $90,000 out of Panama in 2023... That profile still holds true after he slashed .283/.341/.462 in his first three pro seasons and reached High-A at 18. The Twins acquired him in a package for Jhoan Duran last July."
Ford has been traded from Seattle to Washington after becoming surplus following Cal Raleigh’s emergence: "Regarded as the Mariners' catcher of the future when they drafted him 12th overall in 2021... He actually posted the best numbers (.283/.408/.460) of his full-season career in 2025..."
Ethan Salas remains one prospect worth watching despite injuries limiting his playing time since signing with San Diego: "He still has the upside of a Gold Glove catcher with 20-homer power once he's healthy and gets a chance to catch his breath."
